plan.title: AD lesional vs control DE + hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq (Salmon-derived raw gene-level counts, 12000 genes x 13 columns incl. gene symbol, 12 samples: 6 lesional AD skin vs 6 control skin, unpaired, single batch). One sample (sample_01) has a library size ~4x below the median, which threatens both size-factor estimation and per-gene dispersion if left unaddressed. The plan therefore: (1) loads and QC-checks the count matrix and metadata, quantifying the low-depth sample's impact (library size distribution, gene detection rate) and deciding whether to downweight, flag, or exclude it based on objective thresholds rather than assumption; (2) runs a standard DESeq2-equivalent (pydeseq2) negative-binomial differential expression between AD-lesional and control, using size-factor normalization (which is robust to moderate depth differences) and reporting the flagged sample's leverage via Cook's distance / outlier diagnostics rather than silently dropping it; (3) takes the resulting ranked gene list (all genes, ranked by signed statistic) into GSEA preranked against the 50 MSigDB human hallmark gene sets to identify hallmark pathways altered between conditions; (4) produces a compact set of decision-ready outputs (DE table, MA/volcano plot, hallmark enrichment table and plot) with explicit reporting of the low-depth sample's influence on results. All scripting is Python per user constraint (pydeseq2 for DE, gseapy for GSEA prerank), using the MSigDB human hallmark GMT staged in the reference store.
